Well, JumpListExplorer doesn't work for me, even though I installed .NET SDK 9.0 as well, as per its requirements, but I managed to run the command line version. It's interesting, because the "AI" from my phone provided some other results that mentioned the taskbar button arrangement in HKEY_CURRENT_USER\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\Taskband, and thumbnail actions not being stored permanently on disk or the registry, but being programmatic and created on the fly by the Windows API's ITaskbarList3:TumbBarAddButtons interface (probably what you used as well). It said that when opening the app, the app registers those actions in the OS' active memory, and when closing the app, the thumbnail actions dissapear completely. Of course, wasn't interested in the previews, just the commands in them (the .json created by JLECmd has some of those, albeit I tested only on some existing .customDestinations-ms from yesterday that I'm not even sure it included the progress bar thumbnail actions).

In any case, there is no chance of easy editing those task / thumbnail actions and make them run directly something anyway, thus the plugin is still the best bet in that regard. Not sure if there are many use cases where you'd want to run directly something without involving the Rainmeter executable though, so that's debatable.

entry.title: Community Plugins & Addons • Re: AppWindow [skins as normal windows]
entry.content:
Good to know. Well, I didn't refer to setting them dynamically from inside the skin, but to whether there's an easy alternative way to set those task commands to something not involving Rainmeter acting as an intermediary executable, from outside Rainmeter or the skin - e.g. from the shortcut's or .lnk's properties, afterwards (if not, then the only way would be from the skin, and then the plugin should probably provide a way to not involve running Rainmeter, if desired by the user, I guess).

My current use case that I prefer for now is to use the plugin to trigger the creation of the .lnk as an "implicit" button, but copy that .lnk to someplace else and work with it as a "normal" (not "implicit") shortcut afterwards, that can be automatically e.g. deleted from the taskbar folder on unpinning. Obviously, the main role of the plugin is to provide window like capabilities like minimize / restore / etc., but on the shortcut side I personally only use it in the initial phase, so to speak (at least for now).
By the way, I just tried using the plugin with my WebView Earth skin, via some simple:

Code: 

[AppWindow]Measure=PluginPlugin=AppWindowAutoStart=1WindowTitle=#CURRENTCONFIG#WindowIcon=#@#FavIcon.icoAppId=#CURRENTCONFIG#TaskbarDisplayName=#CURRENTCONFIG#TaskbarCommand=[!Launch][!ActivateConfig "#CURRENTCONFIG#"]TaskbarIcon=#@#FavIcon.ico
added to the skin's .ini, and it works wonderfully - the Earth in the skin keeps rotating while minimized, can be seen rotating in the taskbar preview, and all those goodies, I like it. I should probably have some use for the tasks and especially the thumbnail buttons (for e.g. pause, resume, toggle rotation type from Live aka based on actual earth position, to Time aka based on some arbitrary rotation or datetime), but I'll leave that for another time. It's great to have it as an "app like" thingy on the taskbar and manageable like a window though, even if I don't yet and probably won't bother to make specific minimize / close buttons in the skin, due to space constraints and keeping symmetries there.

entry.title: Community Plugins & Addons • Re: AppWindow [skins as normal windows]
entry.content:
Unlike TaskbarCommand, TaskbarTaskCommand can be set dynamically without issues. The only thing to consider is that they’re “shared” between all skins using the same AppID. So if you set different task commands for different skins that group together using the same AppID, the very last set will be the ones being displayed when you right click. This is why is recommended to set the taskbar options to the same values on all skins grouped together by using an included .inc file as I did on the suite example.

entry.title: Community Plugins & Addons • Re: AppWindow [skins as normal windows]
entry.content:
Doing that would cause issues. Windows relies on both AppID and the application path to choose what windows to group. If you do that, the skin will not actually group on that, because it will recognize the shortcut (and thus the taskbar icon) as a shortcut for the calculator and not for the skin. This is why it already includes Rainmeter’s path, I noticed those issues from the beginning.

Remember that those options are not for a simple command, but to create the actual shortcut. On the latest version will default to “…\Rainmeter.exe” [!ActivateConfig “#CURRENTCONFIG#”] when empty. This is because leaving it empty can also confuse Windows, making it group normal Rainmeter windows as well.

However, we can do what you suggest for TaskbarTaskCommand instead, which right now also includes Rainmeter’s path, but could allow to launch whatever application.
Oh, I see... well, if there isn't another / later / easy method to freely customize the TaskbarTaskCommands (like it's available for the shorcut target aka TaskbarCommand, which can be easily edited at will in Windows afterwards), it might be something to think about and see what choice is better, indeed. Can't think of any example where one might actually need such freedom in setting these things at this time, but that doesn't mean it couldn't be something that users may want at some point, for whatever reasons.

P.S. Just to be clear, my point here was to bring this to your attention - I don't have a strong preference for one way or the other. Right now my use of the plugin is for fun and coolness (it's really nice to enjoy!), the actual practical usage scenarios that I may or may not confront in the future with it are yet to come.
